transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat way more than I mean to. It usually starts after work, like after I’m grading papers, I’ll have some leftovers… and then it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter, whatever snacks I had packed for my classroom. The amount of food scares me, honestly.
When you're eating all of that food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes. Once I start, it feels like I’m not really in control anymore. Part of me is saying, like, “Joan, stop, this is enough,” but I just keep opening things and eating them anyway, until I’m painfully full.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like your work or relationships?

Yes, it really does. My evenings and even weekends end up kind of revolving around trying to make up for what happened with food. I’m slower getting grading done, I cancel or sort of zone out with friends, and at work I’m constantly trying to seem like I have everything together when I don’t feel that way.
